findings.reason: retiring the flag as written breaks those two cases, so the section must name them (and either update them to construct the legacy form another way or keep a private entry point), which its own "names every call site it checked" promise currently does not cover.
findings.text: the section retires the public `legacy` keyword from `plan_fingerprint` on the claim that it is a parameter "which nothing outside that helper passes", but two call sites outside `_fingerprint_forms` do pass it: `tests/test_review_plan_command.py:230` and `tests/test_plan_review_store.py:486` both call `plan_fingerprint(..., legacy=True)`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 hides section enumeration, identity, extent and the replaced span behind one raw-text parser and rewrites the walks onto it; §16 keeps one public identity (`plan_fingerprint` returns the same digest) while moving per-section granularity into the private `_authored_prose` walk and a module-private coverage predicate over `read_plan_review`; §18 adds one hoisted reader. Net public-definition change is at most +1, stated in §18, with no spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the recurring duplicates are named with their owner and consolidating mechanism: §18 names the two `c-run-` prefix owners (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:7209 _LANDING_COMMENT_PREFIX` and `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:123 RUN_COMMENT_PREFIX`) and hoists both the constant and the recogniser to `reckon/_store.py`; §17 names the two raw-text span implementations (the store's `_H2_OPEN_RE`/`_SECTION_OPEN_RE`/`_matching_section_close` in `reckon/_store.py` and `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`) and collapses the store onto the parser. No finding: the plan extends owners rather than forking them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 correctly states it adds no public definition and adds none to the other three families, but its stated accounting of what it retires is wrong (see the finding below), so the retirement half of the rule is not satisfied as written.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — each section cites and extends a mechanism that already exists rather than proposing new machinery: §17 extends `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py` and reuses the private-rule pattern in `reckon/interface_counts.py` (`read_trees`, `definitions`, `_staged_writes`); §16 extends `plan_fingerprint`/`_AuthoredProseParser` and `_fingerprint_forms` in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`; §18 hoists `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` to `reckon/_store.py` and reuses `landed_section_ids`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 argues explicitly that the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (it joins a set of outstanding sections to the union of stored digests) and names why nothing is retired; §17 extends the existing parser instead of adding a parallel scanner; §18 extends the store rather than forking it.
